stories.title: Long-term air pollution exposure and childhood ADHD prevalence
stories.description: Fine particulate air pollution ($$\hbox {PM}_{2.5}$$) in the United States has fallen by roughly half since 2000, yet health outcomes may reflect pollution exposures accumulated over longer time scales. Using years of U.S. county-level data, we relate annual $$\hbox {PM}_{2.5}$$ estimates to birth outcomes, diabetes prevalence, and small-area estimates of childhood attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) across short and long time scales. Whereas associations with low birth weight and the apparent lag pattern for diabetes were substantially attenuated after accounting for county-specific temporal trends, the association between long-term $$\hbox {PM}_{2.5}$$ exposure and childhood ADHD prevalence across 3,106 counties remained robust to socioeconomic and demographic adjustment, state-level heterogeneity, alternative exposure periods, and explicit spatial modeling. After accounting for residual spatial dependence, a 1 $$\mu$$g/$$\hbox {m}^3$$ increase in mean $$\hbox {PM}_{2.5}$$ exposure over 2005–2015 was associated with a 0.312 percentage-point higher ADHD prevalence (SE = 0.058, $$p < 0.001$$). These results identify a robust ecological association between long-term county-level $$\hbox {PM}_{2.5}$$ exposure and childhood ADHD prevalence across the United States.

stories.title: PSEG improves human pose estimation via plug-and-play structural edge guidance
stories.description: Human pose estimation in dense occlusion suffers from keypoint misdetection and joint misalignment. Existing methods struggle to exploit structural edge constraints owing to the lack of high-quality human edge data and dedicated detectors. We propose PSEG (Plug-and-Play Structural Edge Guidance), a framework that addresses occlusion in crowded multi-person pose estimation. We introduce PSEG-Bench, the first large-scale 2D multi-person edge dataset generated via SMPL projection with APDC-RPDC adaptive morphological optimization, providing reliable supervision. We develop a lightweight PSEG module trained by semi-supervised learning using 200,000 real unlabeled frames to bridge the synthetic-to-real domain gap between SMPL-projected and real edges, with dynamic confidence thresholds. Ablation studies verify that our input-end single-scale injection adds only 2.39% parameters while outperforming multi-scale injection; the loss weight α = 1.1 optimally balances edge-background class imbalance, while reward-driven and gradient consistency constraints suppress Canny-induced noise. Strict non-overlapping dataset partitioning eliminates data leakage. Under motion blur (σ = 5) and low-light (γ = 0.5) degradation, PSEG delivers up to 6.4 AP recovery. On OCHuman, it yields 1.2–2.1% absolute AP gain. On CrowdPose, PSEG improves HRNet and TransPose by 0.8–2.6 AP (average 1.52). On MSCOCO, it boosts mAP by 1.1–2.5 (average 1.62). Experiments show that PSEG suppresses false activations and accelerates convergence. Code: https://github.com/wilson-up1/PSEG-main.
